leader.line: Born in Iran. Fled to Sweden at six. Co-founded Databricks.
leader.story: Ali Ghodsi was born in Iran in 1978. His family fled to Sweden when he was six, where he grew up and earned a PhD in distributed systems at KTH. As a visiting scholar at UC Berkeley he helped create Apache Spark, co-founded Databricks in 2013, and has run it since 2016.

holdings.name: Novo Nordisk

leader.line: Fled Iran at 12. Started as a clerk. Now runs Novo Nordisk.
leader.story: Mike Doustdar fled Iran at 12 and joined Novo Nordisk in 1992 as an office clerk in Vienna. Over three decades he rose through finance, logistics, and international operations across 150 countries before becoming President and CEO in 2025.

holdings.thesis: Iranian-born Maziar Mike Doustdar became CEO of Novo Nordisk in August 2025, the first non-Dane to lead the company since 1923. Backed by a 51% operating margin and a +30 percentage point ROIC-WACC spread across its GLP-1 metabolic franchise, Novo Nordisk trades at a compelling valuation multiple.

holdings.name: AppLovin

leader.line: Born in Iran. Fled the war as a child. Co-founded AppLovin.
leader.story: Adam Foroughi was born in Iran in 1980 and came to America as a child when his family fled the Iran-Iraq War. He grew up in Laguna Niguel, California, studied economics at UC Berkeley, and traded derivatives before co-founding AppLovin in 2012. He took the company public in 2021 and continues to lead it as Chairman and CEO.

holdings.thesis: Adam Foroughi co-founded AppLovin in 2012 and scaled AXON into the dominant AI ad-monetization engine in mobile gaming and e-commerce. With 78% operating margins, 52% free-cash-flow margins, and 55%+ revenue growth, AppLovin earns the highest return on invested capital in the PRSN universe.

holdings.name: Uber Technologies

leader.line: Born in Tehran. Ran Expedia for 12 years. Made Uber profitable.
leader.story: Dara Khosrowshahi was born in Tehran in 1969. His family left as the revolution began and rebuilt in New York. After graduating from Brown University, he spent twelve years leading Expedia as CEO before taking over Uber in 2017.

holdings.thesis: Since taking over as CEO in 2017, Dara Khosrowshahi transformed Uber from a cash-burning rideshare startup into a global mobility and delivery powerhouse generating 17% free-cash-flow margins, a +9 percentage point ROIC spread, and aggressive share repurchases.

holdings.name: Teledyne Technologies

leader.line: Born in Tehran. MIT doctorate. Led Carnegie Mellon, then Teledyne.
leader.story: Robert Mehrabian was born in Tehran in 1941 and earned his bachelor's and doctorate degrees at MIT. A materials scientist, he served as president of Carnegie Mellon University from 1990 to 1997, then led Teledyne as CEO from its 1999 spin-off through 2018 before becoming Executive Chairman.

holdings.thesis: Teledyne compounds capital through high-margin digital imaging, subsea instrumentation, aerospace, and defense electronics. Under Robert Mehrabian's disciplined capital allocation, the company generates steady 20% operating margins and resilient free cash flow across cycles.

holdings.name: Intuit

leader.line: Arrived from Tehran at nine. Engineer. CEO of Intuit since 2019.
leader.credit: Photo: Intuit Corp., CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
leader.story: Sasan Goodarzi came to the United States from Tehran at nine during the revolution and finished high school in Orlando. An electrical engineer with a Kellogg MBA, he worked at Honeywell and Invensys, joined Intuit in 2004, and became CEO in 2019.

holdings.thesis: Sasan Goodarzi has led Intuit since 2019 across TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma, and Mailchimp. Combining 40% free-cash-flow margins with a +18 percentage point ROIC-WACC spread, Intuit anchors the Core sleeve at an attractive forward valuation.

holdings.name: Prologis

leader.line: Left Tehran at 14. MIT at 16. Built the world's largest logistics landlord.
leader.story: Hamid Moghadam left Tehran at 14, finished school in Switzerland, and arrived at MIT at 16. After earning a Stanford MBA, he co-founded AMB in 1983 and merged it with ProLogis in 2011 to create the largest logistics real estate company in the world.

holdings.thesis: Co-founded by Hamid Moghadam in 1983, Prologis is the world's preeminent industrial logistics REIT. With 51% free-cash-flow margins and irreplaceable urban warehouse land banks increasingly monetized for hyperscale AI data centers, Prologis provides durable real-asset cash flow.

holdings.name: Marcus & Millichap

leader.line: Born in Tehran. Joined as a research analyst; became CEO in 2016.
leader.story: Hessam Nadji was born in Tehran and immigrated to the United States as a teenager. He joined Marcus & Millichap in 1996 as Vice President of Research, architected the firm's national specialty brokerage expansion, and was appointed President and CEO in 2016.

holdings.thesis: Led by Tehran-born CEO Hessam Nadji, Marcus & Millichap is North America's leading middle-market commercial real estate investment brokerage. The firm maintains a fortress net-cash balance sheet that positions it for strong operating leverage as transaction volumes recover.

holdings.name: Monarch Casino & Resort

leader.line: Born in Tehran. Built Atlantis Reno and Monarch Black Hawk.
leader.story: John Farahi was born in Tehran and immigrated to the United States, where he and his brothers Bob and Ben acquired a small Reno motel in 1972 and built it into Monarch Casino & Resort, taking the company public on Nasdaq in 1993.

holdings.thesis: Co-founded and led by Tehran-born John Farahi, Monarch Casino & Resort operates luxury destination resorts in Reno and Black Hawk. With 27% operating margins, minimal net leverage, and consistent capital returns, Monarch is one of the highest-quality balance sheets in hospitality.

holdings.name: Reservoir Media

leader.line: Founded Reservoir in 2007. First female Iranian-Canadian music publishing CEO.
leader.story: Golnar Khosrowshahi's family left Iran following the 1979 revolution. Educated at Bryn Mawr and Columbia University, she founded Reservoir Media in 2007 and built it into the first female-founded, publicly traded independent music company in the US.

holdings.thesis: Founded by Golnar Khosrowshahi in 2007, Reservoir Media owns and manages over 150,000 music copyrights generating recurring royalty cash flows with 21.5% operating margins.

holdings.name: Biglari Holdings

leader.line: Born in Tehran. Built a permanent-capital holding company in San Antonio.
leader.story: Sardar Biglari was born in Tehran in 1977; his family left Iran in 1984 and settled in Texas. He founded Biglari Capital at age 22 and took control of Steak 'n Shake in 2008, transforming it into Biglari Holdings.

holdings.thesis: Led by Tehran-born Sardar Biglari, Biglari Holdings operates a permanent-capital holding company across restaurant brands, commercial insurance, and energy royalties, generating an 18% free-cash-flow margin.

holdings.name: Life Time Group

leader.line: Left Tehran at 17. Bet everything on one club in 1992.
leader.story: Bahram Akradi left Tehran at 17 in 1978, worked in restaurants to pay for an electrical engineering degree at the University of Colorado, and entered the health-club industry. In 1992 he sold everything he owned to open one club in Brooklyn Park, Minnesota, which grew into Life Time.

holdings.thesis: Bahram Akradi founded Life Time in 1992 and built it into North America's premier athletic country club operator. Strong membership pricing power, 17% operating margins, and expanding sale-leaseback capital recycling drive consistent double-digit revenue and earnings growth.

holdings.name: Guardant Health

leader.line: Studied in Tehran and Stanford. Pioneered liquid biopsy cancer screening.
leader.story: AmirAli Talasaz studied electrical engineering at Sharif University of Technology in Tehran before completing his PhD at Stanford, where he invented non-invasive blood-testing technologies and co-founded Guardant Health in 2012.

holdings.thesis: Co-founded and led by Sharif University and Stanford alumnus AmirAli Talasaz, Guardant Health is the category leader in liquid biopsy and blood-based colorectal cancer screening (Shield), scaling revenue at 36% year over year.

holdings.name: ServiceTitan

leader.line: Immigrated from Iran as a child. Built ServiceTitan for tradespeople like his father.
leader.story: Ara Mahdessian immigrated to California from Iran as a young boy and watched his father work as a residential contractor. After studying at Stanford, he co-founded ServiceTitan in 2012 to build enterprise software for trades businesses and took it public on Nasdaq in 2024.

holdings.thesis: Co-founded by Iranian-Armenian immigrant Ara Mahdessian, ServiceTitan is the operating system for the trades. Generating 21% revenue growth and expanding positive free-cash-flow margins, ServiceTitan compounds high-retention vertical SaaS and fintech volume.

holdings.name: Tarsus Pharmaceuticals

leader.line: Iranian-American Rhodes Scholar. Founded Tarsus to create a new category in eye care.
leader.story: Dr. Bobak Azamian is a second-generation Iranian-American who earned his bachelor's at Rice, a DPhil at Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar, and his MD at Harvard/MIT before founding Tarsus Pharmaceuticals in 2016.

holdings.thesis: Founded by Iranian-American physician-scientist Bobak Azamian, Tarsus commercialized XDEMVY, the first FDA-approved treatment for Demodex blepharitis, driving 64%+ revenue growth and rapid operating leverage.

schemes.name: PRSN method
schemes.note: Score only, no size, momentum, 5–20% limits

conclusions: Weighting: Same, no momentum had the best risk-adjusted return (Sharpe 0.59). Our method ranks 2 of 7 at 0.57, after 10 bp trading costs.

Momentum: it made little difference over this period (Sharpe 0.57 with vs 0.59 without). Names in the top half on 12-month momentum beat the bottom half the next month 55% of the time, by +0.8 pts on average.

Trend: names above their 200-day average returned +2.8% the following month on average, vs +2.9% for names below it. That's no real edge, so the 200-day line is shown for context, not used in the weights.

Rebalancing: annual scored best (Sharpe 0.80), but the gaps between cadences are within noise for 57 months of data. Monthly plus a drift trigger keeps weights within 5 points of the rules and trades about 65% of the portfolio a year.
Macro: PRSN averaged +4.4% a month when the 10-year yield fell and -0.5% when it rose. It's a rate-sensitive basket.
Diversification: average correlation between holdings is 0.13 over the past year.

changelog.note: Initial six-factor equal-tilt model (5-20% weights, monthly + 5-pt drift).
Introduced three-pillar conviction tiers and a strict 3-month -20% relative price stop across all holdings.

Ackman-style high-conviction compounder & catalyst model. Removed the mechanical 3-month relative price stop on profitable compounders after post-mortem analysis showed it forced premature exits in high-ROIC leaders (e.g., AppLovin, Novo Nordisk) during short-term pullbacks. Expanded the universe with verified NYSE/Nasdaq Persian-led companies (Monarch Casino, Marcus & Millichap, Lesaka, AudioEye, Bluerock) and calibrated sizing across 14 high-conviction positions (~64% in 5 Core anchors, ~26% in 5 Build compounders, and ~10% in 4 Catalyst sleeves).

rules.heritage: CEO, co-CEO or executive chair of Persian heritage, full or partial: born in Iran, or with Iranian roots through family, of any ethnicity or faith. Documented by a public source, never inferred from a name.

wildcard.rule: Scaled high-growth innovators qualify directly through the Catalyst sleeve ($3B+ market cap and 30%+ revenue growth or positive FCF)
Fastest revenue growth among eligible, liquid, pre-profit companies over the size floor
